$comment: The deck plan of High Office (docs/design/office-style.md, section 8). Generated by scratchpad/office/content/mkplan.py (not in the repository; edit by hand from now on if that file is gone); the comedy editor owns it. scripts/content/office/check.ts reads it to tell a writer which quotas their batch still misses. Counts are of records; "cells" keys are "<club>.<archetype>". Ids and tag names are format.ts's.

setup.premise: Scripted paper 4: Lionel Sash's fruit basket "No reason". Both follow-ups are written (7.6 A).
The prize pumpkin is granted the freedom of the town (7.6 B).
The 7:02 bus is named after you; it is late and it waves.
A museum of old bus tickets opens in the disused ticket office.
The Spotters pay for the clock tower to chime at every bus time, not only the hours.
You are asked to judge Window Week, the Guild's display contest.
The Guild pays to string bunting from the clock tower to every shop.
A new signpost to the high street that points both ways, for fairness.
The Society names its prize turnip after you.
A scarecrow for the patch, built in your likeness, to scare the crows (and, hopefully, the spotters).
The weigh-in moves to the bus station forecourt for the day.
The Guild takes the bandstand for Window Week displays; the pumpkin show must wait.
The band practises on the anglers' jetty.
The Anglers rent one Sunday of silence.
A floating bench on the canal, so anglers can sit where the fish are.
You conduct the band for one bar.
A small bandstand for the tuba alone, so it can practise without the others.
The Spotters pay to name a bus shelter after their founder's notebook.
You open Till's new tea room with a single, photographed sip.
A Glasshouse Office glasshouse for a single prize pumpkin.
The vegetable show takes the canal towpath for a day.
A new bus stop right beside the bandstand.
You hold the Circle's ceremonial float for the Evening Fuss photograph.
The band pays to have its practice listed as a public event.
Kitewell is built a hill.
A modest hedge is clipped in your likeness and you pose beside it.
The Kitewell hedge maze is declared free of kites.
The League books the wind over Brassby for an afternoon.
You launch the first kite of the season.
A hedge is clipped into a clock that tells the time, roughly.
The band plays on the harbour steps at Saltpenny Bay, where the anglers sit.
A lighthouse that dims itself so as not to disturb the fish.
A bench beside the motorway for watching coaches go by.
Till's Teas sponsors the Lamplight Authority: every lamp glows the colour of tea.
The national prize pumpkin tours the provinces and you ride beside it.
The Committee pays to judge your official lawn edges.
